ear: A part of the head (or face) used for hearing.
My rabbit has two big ears.
earth: I planted some roses in this patch of earth.
Anything made up mostly of rock, sand or soil.
Earth is the third planet from the sun, where we live.
A planet, especially one like Earth.
He came from a different earth.
One of the four classical elements.
One of the five Taoist elements.
The planet on which we live – the third planet of the Solar System.
The moon goes around the Earth.
each: all or every one in a group separately
Come here you two. I'll give each of you a toy.
early: If something is early, it is sooner than expected.
It was an early end to the meeting.
If something is early, it happens in the first part of a time period.
He didn't like going to the early classes.
He was at the meeting early.
During the first part of a time period.
She got up early in the morning.
east: The east is a place that is closer to where the sun rises than another place.
My parents live in the east.
One of the four compass directions: 90º clockwise from north. The sun rises in the east.
eagle: He saw an eagle perched on top of that tree.
An old gold coin in the United States worth $10.
He showed me his coin collection. He even had an old eagle.
A score of two under par for a hole.
I got a birdy and you got an eagle on that last hole.
If you eagle a golf hole, you score two under par on it.
I eagled the last hole with 3 strokes on a par 5.
eat: If you eat something, usually food, you put it in your mouth, chew it, and swallow it.
I always eat too much good when it's Thanksgiving.
If you eat the cost of something, you pay for it.
The supplier will have to eat the cost of returning the goods.
If you eat someone, you give them sex with your mouth (oral sex)
easy: If something is easy, it does not need much skill or effort.
The teacher gave an easy test to her students.
If something is easy, it is comfortable.
I had to get out of my easy chair in order to open the door for our guests.
If you do something easy, you do slowly, without effort, calmly.
Take it easy. (See also take it easy.)
eater: An eater eats something. An eater of x, eats mostly x.
earthward: Moving in the direction of or facing the earth
earn: If you earn something you get it by working or doing something.
I earn a lot more money at my new job than at my last job.
If you think you have earned something, you think you should have it because of what you have done.
After completing that project I thought I had earned some time to rest.
easter: Easter is a Christian celebration, usually in April, of the day when Christians believe that Jesus of Nazareth came back from the dead.
Our church will start Easter Sunday with a sunrise service at 6 a.m.
earthquake: An earthquake is a natural event that causes the ground to shake up and down, and sometimes, may destroy buildings.
The earthquake ripped a crack in the road and destroyed half of the building that I live in.
earthwork: An earthwork is a construction made of earth, especially to protect an area from attack.
The existing walls and buildings were linked together with earthworks.
earring: An earring is a piece of jewelry worn on the ear.
earthen: If something is earthen, it is made of earth or mud.
The earthen walls of the house were very thick.
If something is earthen, it is made of clay (usually said of pottery).
The earthen dishes were easily chipped or broken.
If something is earthen, it is the color of earth, soil or dirt.
The walls of the buildings in Timbuktu are the same earthen color as the sand and soil of central Mali.
ease: n
The state of being comfortable or relaxed.
She enjoyed the ease of living in a house where the servants did all the work.
n
from pain, worry, etc.
His mind was at ease when he took the test. He knew he had studied well.
n
Free from effort, difficulty or hardship.
He passed all the exams with ease.
n
Doing something without much effort.
He played the piano with ease.
n
To be free from money problems.
After winning the lottery, she lived a life of ease.
n
, rest and leisure.
We took our ease on the patio.
v
To free or lessen (something) from pain, worry, agitation, etc.
He eased his conscience telling her what he had done wrong.
v
To loosen or relax the tension on (something).
We eased the rope, then lowered the sail.
v
To reduce the difficulty of (something).
We had to ease the entry requirements.
v
To move (something) slowly and carefully.
He eased the car into the parking space.
eastern: Of, facing, situated in, or related to the east.
Washington, D.C. is on the eastern side of United States.
easel: An easel is a wooden frame for holding a painted picture.
The artist set up his easel by the bank of the river.
eager: To be eager is to hardly be able to wait to do something.
They were eager to see the new movie.
easterly: An easterly is any continuous wind from the east.
If something or someone is easterly, they are facing east.
The boat was taking an easterly course towards its destination.
If a place is easterly, it can be found to the east.
The cabin can be found of the easterly side of the lake.
If something is easterly, it comes from the east.
The wind is an easterly wind.
If something is done easterly, it is done towards the east.
easily: If you do something easily, you have no trouble doing it.
If something could easily happen, it is likely.
earnest: If someone is earnest, they are serious and truly believe in what they say or do.
earbud: ; An earbud is a small headphone that you put in your ear.
I use earbuds for listening to music.
earthworm: An earthworm is a type of worm that lives in the ground.
When it was raining, the earthworms came out.
eavesdrop: If you eavesdrop on a conversation, you secretly listen to it without anyone knowing.
I hope nobody was eavesdropping on our conversation last night, since it got so personal.
earl: An earl is a British or Irish nobleman next in rank above a viscount and below a marquess; equivalent to a European count. A female using the style is termed a countess.
earldom: Earldom is the rank of being an earl.
Earldom is the territory controlled by an earl.
earthy: If something is earthy, it is like dirt or soil.
If a person is earthy, they are honest and direct about a topic they are talking about.
earnings: Your earnings is the amount of money you obtain from doing something.
All my earnings for the year wouldn't cover the cost of one of her designer dresses.
eatery: An eatery is a restaurant or café.
earful: If you give someone an earful, you scold or reprimand them.
earthly: If something is earthly, it is related to the Earth.
eaves: The eaves of a building is the underside of its roof that extends beyond the external walls of it.
eastbound: If you are travelling eastbound, you are travelling towards the east.
earmuff: A earmuff is a garment worn over the ears to keep it warm.
A earmuff is a protective equipment that is worn over the ears to protect it from loud sounds.
earnestly: If something is done earnestly, it is done in a earnest manner.
eagerly: If something is done eagerly, it is done in an eager manner.
easygoing: An easygoing person is someone who is calm, casual and informal.
easy-going: An easy-going person is someone who is calm, casual and informal.
earphone: A earphone is a very small headphone that is fitted into a person's ear that makes sound.
The music on the person's earphones was so loud that he didn't know I was talking to him.
earshot: If a person is within earshot, they are at a distance where sound can still be heard.
easiness: The easiness of something is how easy it is.
eagerness: The eagerness of someone is how eager they are.
earache: An earache is a pain in your ears.
ear-ring: An ear-ring is a piece of jewelry worn on the ear.
easterner: A easterner is a person or thing that is from the east of a place.
